sources.scope: Selected actual species diagnosis read: short unarmed rounded rostrum, stout subchelate first pereiopod, smaller second pair, smooth sixth pleonite, paired scaphocerites and small telson-spine cues. No source dimensions or fine anatomical measurements fitted.

sources.title: Arnott, Neil & Ansell1998 — brown-shrimp tail-flip mechanism
sources.scope: Selected actual paper pages1–2/5–6 read and page6 Fig3/4 viewed. Escape involves anterior abdominal and cephalothorax flex, expanded scaphocerite head-fan and tail-fan, and often roll. This model offers only mild local flex, not that full measured escape mechanism; rates, coordinates, forces and trajectories are not imported.

retrieval.accessMethod: Selected actual primary PDF text and rendered figures

findings.shape: Distinct flattened broad cephalothorax with a short unarmed rounded rostrum, continuous tapering abdomen, smooth sixth dorsal somite, stout first-pair subchelae and smaller second-pair chelae. Six posterior main walking limbs support the body. Separate antennal scales, five simple pleopod pairs, a telson and four uropodal lobes replace the same rounded draft used for the prawn.
findings.surface: Original brown/cream fine mottling and darker fan ends replace a flat beige draft. The initial overly pale coarse speckling was reduced. Selected pigmentation is not a calibrated chromatophore state, scan, or photograph texture; fine dorsal segment boundaries and natural optical variation remain weak.
findings.movement: Same-model fixed-length support/recovery and stopping, local subchela/antenna gestures, simple pleopod articulation and mild serial flex are available. The full escape is explicitly unavailable: an upright tail bend does not reproduce the studied body roll, cephalothorax/abdomen jackknife and head-fan mechanism.
findings.evidenceScope: Authentic Holger Krisp CC BY3.0 photo compared with selected actual Naturalis diagnosis and MarLIN species context. Selected primary Arnott, Neil and Ansell1998 pages1–2/5–6 and actual page6 Figures3/4 were reviewed for escape scope; measured coordinates, rates, size dependence and trajectories were not imported.
corrections: Separated the broad flatter shrimp profile from the laterally compressed prawn and replaced repeated rounded tail sections with one persistent deforming cuticle.
Added a short unarmed rostrum, stout P1 subchelae, smaller P2, antennal scales and simple serial swimmeret/fan articulation.
Reduced excessive white surface speckling seen in the first top view.
Replaced the flat lid-like frontal closure with convex cuticle and partial mouthpart cues after actual enlarged comparison.
Kept Escape disabled and labelled the mild flex as a partial study instead of presenting it as measured escape biomechanics.
findings.residual: Still partly stylized: head cuticle is too smooth in places, mottling and dorsal somite separation remain approximate, and ventral anatomy, fan rays/setae, fine spine positions and actual chromatophore changes are incomplete. Limb segmentation and support order are authored, not species-measured. No swimming trajectory, full escape, feeding or hydrodynamics; no independent biological validation.
